failureClassification.method: Every one of the 11 failed attempts was classified mechanically from its own frozen evidence: the per-task result record (exception, effectiveAgentTimeoutSec, durationMs, pierExitCode, modelOutcomes) plus its best-agent-evidence.jsonl (model-request and model-outcome counts, model-failure entries). No classification was inferred from the verifier, from logs, or from prose.
failureClassification.finding: The count of model-failure entries is 0 in all 11 failed attempts; model requests and outcomes are equal or differ by exactly one (the request the harness cut at the budget boundary); pierExitCode is 0 for all 11; the aggregate report records 0 error and 0 not-evaluated cells. No task in run 36092882496 failed for an upstream/provider or an environment reason. The only rerun-eligible failures are the 3 agent-budget timeouts below.

notRerun.reason: Each ended with terminalCause completed well inside its own budget (3025s/5400s, 2459s/5400s, 1606s/5400s, 646s/900s, 651s/1800s, 215s/900s, 441s/900s), with zero model-failure entries and a real graded verifier result (f2p 78/79, 0/94, 28/31, and reward=0 respectively). These are genuine capability outcomes of the agent, not upstream, timeout or environment effects, so they are not rerun: re-running a genuine model failure to obtain a different verdict is best-of-N / rescue and is prohibited by the repository's benchmark rules.

Pre-declared in config/frontier-harness.json#specificationGaps: the task's pinned instruction omits a rule its hidden tests require. The attempt itself was a real model outcome (252 model outcomes, 252/252 answered, 4077s/5400s, terminalCause completed) and the aggregate report already excludes this task from capability comparisons. A rerun cannot repair a frozen task defect, and the source run's own classification leaves its verdict standing unchanged.

batches.reason: User-authorized rerun of the failures whose cause is a timeout. Each task carries an existing canonical verdict (failed) in run 36092882496, so this batch is a variance probe only and can never replace or reinterpret those verdicts. Mechanical classification of the timeout: all three attempts ended on AgentTimeoutError at their own official 900s agent budget (947s, 930s, 933s) while the agent was still iterating, and every one of the three frozen attempt evidences contains zero model-failure entries (chess-best-move 35 requests / 35 outcomes, gcode-to-text 49/48, largest-eigenval 21/20 — the single unanswered request in the last two is the one cut at the budget boundary). The agent was killed at the budget boundary, not by a provider transport or connection failure. The timeout is chronic across candidates: the same tasks also hit their official budget in run 35992545942 (candidate d631b623/beta.33), where chess-best-move passed inside budget in the diagnostic rerun 36005393416 and the other two reproduced their timeout. In run 36092882496 the fourth chronic task, terminal-bench/code-from-image, completed inside its own budget and passed, so it is not in this batch. The official agent budget is preserved (fh_agent_timeout_multiplier=1); it is never extended to convert a budget outcome into a pass.

batches.reason: Every one of the 11 cells that failed in run 36092882496 is re-measured on a NEW candidate (0.0.3-beta.36 / c9ae2e2f), which is the first candidate that carries spec 241: bounded per-call call times in the attempt evidence. This is a measurement of the new candidate, not a rescue of the old verdicts. Two questions only: (a) does each failure reproduce on a different candidate, and (b) where did each attempt's wall clock actually go. Question (b) could not be answered from any earlier artifact at all: every elapsed-time figure in the previous records is a derivation (a waitMs sum, or durationMs divided by the model-call count), and a request the harness cut at the budget boundary carried no time bound whatsoever. The new candidate changes measurement and naming only: spec 241 records two bounded integers on an existing record variant, and the runner-side B1 conformance renames an attempt-derived ceiling without changing its value. No task-visible behaviour, tool surface, instruction text or budget changes, so this batch is expected to measure variance rather than improvement, and it cannot support any capability claim.

batches.splitReason: The workflow refuses more than 10 predeclared tasks per run ("Each workflow run must preselect between 1 and 10 tasks."), so the 11 declared cells are dispatched as two parts. The parts run sequentially on purpose: two concurrent runs would put up to 16 model calls in flight against the same provider, and the whole point of this batch is a clean measurement, so the frozen conditions of the source run (fh_max_parallel=8, one run at a time) are preserved. Part A holds the six longest-budget cells and part B the five shorter ones.

measuredCallDurations.note: Same measurement as part A (spec 241): startedAtMs on each model-request record, durationMs on its matching model-outcome or model-failure. calls = model-request records, including a request cut at the budget boundary; closures = requests with a matching outcome. Model share = sum of per-call durations / agent wall clock.
measuredCallDurations.finding: Model-call time is 77-96% of the agent wall clock on every cell, so tool and process waits are the minority. The hypothesis that recovering wasted tool waits would flip a timeout verdict is not supported by measurement: on db-wal-recovery the model-time sum alone (901s) exceeds the whole 900s budget, and on the two reproduced timeouts the model-time sum is 83% (gcode-to-text, 743s) and 79% (largest-eigenval, 710s) of the budget, while the spread of a single model call (max 190.2s / 208.3s / 578.1s) is far larger than the non-model time that remains. chess-best-move, the cell the earlier ~180s process-polling upper bound was derived from, measured only 56s of non-model time and finished inside its budget.

dispatches.conclusion: 4 of 6 cells flipped to passed on a candidate with no task-affecting change over the source run, which is run-to-run variance rather than improvement; the 2 reproduced failures are both budget outcomes at the official 900s edge. gcode-to-text and largest-eigenval have now hit their official budget in four measured attempts across three candidates (chronic), while chess-best-move and db-wal-recovery flipped. All six attempts again recorded zero model-failure entries with pierExitCode 0, and the part A error cell is resolved as a clean pass. No further rerun is proposed for these cells.

partBAdditions.reason: Explicit upstream provider transport failure, mechanically proven: exactly one model-failure entry with reason=connection, NonZeroAgentExitCodeError, pierExitCode=0, 295 requests against 294 outcomes with 0 unanswered, and a verifier that had run with f2p partial 0.9988. disposition=error, so the cell carries no verdict and nothing is being reinterpreted. The user's standing authorization is to re-run failures caused by upstream problems, timeouts or external factors.
partBAdditions.boundary: This is a diagnostic re-measurement inside a diagnostic batch, not a benchmark-level recovery that fills a formal cell: the attempt produced a model.patch, so the 'no prediction' condition of the recovery rule is not met, and this cell is therefore never treated as a missing formal cell. The error disposition of part A stands as that batch's record and is never overwritten.
